title: Long-Horizon Agents Need Experiments, Not Just Prompts — Erina Karati
talk_summary: The speaker describes an auto-research loop for long-horizon multi-agent systems: controlled scenarios, structured traces, balanced behavioral scorecards, and small policy edits. The loop keeps only changes that improve the scorecard while guardrails hold, with rollback as mandatory.

takeaways.technique: Controlled scenario suite with balanced scorecard
takeaways.what_they_do: Define controlled scenarios, run the full agent system, collect traces, and score multiple behavioral dimensions instead of one vague quality metric.

takeaways.technique: Freeze harness and expose small policy surface
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep scenarios, metrics, and harness fixed; let the optimizer edit only controlled policies like prompts, retrieval, trust, and replanning rules.
takeaways.evidence_quote: freeze the harness, the scenarios, and the metrics

takeaways.what_they_do: Log structured reviewer traces (defects cited, severity, source, decision) and score them against known defects and false positives.
takeaways.evidence_quote: During the run, we collect structured traces

takeaways.technique: Provenance and uncertainty in agent memory
takeaways.what_they_do: Store source and confidence metadata (firsthand/secondhand/verified/uncertain) and separate raw episodic memory from current beliefs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: preserve whether it was firsthand, secondhand, verified or uncertain

takeaways.what_they_do: Test whether agents replan and communicate when the world changes, and measure time to replan and action consistency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Do agents update this and communicate this

takeaways.what_they_do: Try a policy change, score it, keep only if the scorecard improves and guardrails hold; otherwise revert.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Try a change, score it, keep it only if the scorecard improves
